Its alright, this one... Not too complicated, fairly simple actually. Its been a while since I felt the need to renew my 'roster update' subscription for Football Manager after conquering that game over more than fifty seasons a decade ago because its the same game every year at a new price. 

But that is why I pick up games like this, you know I've played a dirty dozen of mobile football management games and this is in the same vein. 

However this game places you more in the role of the owner of the club than the manager or the coaches, which means they get delegated match day tasks while you do the oversight and back-office type of things, at least the mode I'm playing. But there are options to directly intervene in games as well, with the manager reminding you its his job, but once I had to because they were playing too cautiously protecting a lead.

When you're set up for the season you can fly through matches if you want. First season I ended mid-table on lower mid-table requirement and second season I lost by penalties in promotion play-offs with mid-table requirement. 

The game does sort of directly interpret the outcomes of what you do, like if you don't invest in the best striker you can you will score a lot less goals than other teams. Or if you don't have a 58 rated physician but keep your 55 rated physician, your players get more tired and there's not a lot in the middle for the team overcoming things by themselves so far it seems. 

If you want to coach the best teams immediately you have to pay for one of the coaching licences which you also earn by playing well over time. So the monetization is in that or in director coins which you can buy too which you earn like a salary and performance based reward to get like massive investment in your club or whatever.

Ultimately one has to consider the gaming landscape and the few dozen studios that dominate the gaming market except for the few indie titles that slip through to massive success to understand why certain games opt for certain release models. 

While some games will charge you for a skin or lock crucial game mechanics or modes behind paywall, this is not entirely the case here. This is more a game that plays like a story mode where you unlock things that you could buy over time if you wanted to. 

What you get is a fairly simple interface-based game which works to just give you something to click through to keep your mind engaged and occupied for awhile and is football-themed. I do wonder when I sometimes mysteriously lose five games in a row without depth of access to reasoning why, which concerns me regarding parameters of scripting of events. 

You need to believe in the under-lying mechanics for a football simulation to work and be successful. I've seen other football simulations do worse by forcing a link between monetization and on-pitch performance. 

With Football Club Management 2023 you can start out playing it a bit and if you enjoyed it you can toss a few bucks to the devs for appreciation.

I've always yearned for a game that grants me full control over a football club, and this one delivers exactly that. While many games tend to stray into the realm of unrealistic scenarios, this one strikes a perfect balance. You may find yourself losing to supposedly weaker teams, but hey, that's how it goes in real-life football, right? For those who have an unbridled passion for the beautiful game and dream of experiencing what it's like to manage a football club, I wholeheartedly recommend giving this game a try. The best part? You don't have to spend your hard-earned money like in most other games out there. Everything you need can be earned simply by playing. However, as much as this game gets right, there are a few irksome issues that can make it frustrating to play:
1. Player overreactions: It's baffling how players react to fines by wanting to leave every single time.
2. Despite signing top-notch players, having a solid infrastructure, and receiving positive hints, your team may still perform poorly.
3. I've painstakingly built my team from the ground up and achieved the highest ratings, yet I consistently lose to teams that are far less formidable. Sure, having a "bogey team" is one thing, but this takes it to a whole new level of frustration.
4. Our defense, even with exceptional defenders, seems to have an uncanny knack for letting in goals.
5. In European competitions, it's often the case that we face teams from the same league or, when progressing to the knockout rounds, end up against a team from our own group.

Would have liked to play this game but unfortunately they have forgotten to program the save game feature. So it is unplayable. I also wonder what else they didn't program. Not a good sign at all.

Edit: So I really like playing simple football manager games so I try again. Meanwhile I click Chinese in language by accident so my game is now in Chinese. I restart, still Chinese. Now, I click other languages (I think they are other languages at least) nothing happens. So, this game thinks saving games is very optional and just "Ok, whatever", yet keeping track of your chosen language and not letting you change it ever is just paramount. This game's suckiness just got personal. How can you produce such a thing?

Edit2: I have gotten it to work but ended up playing the mobile version for around 30 seasons. It is ok I guess for a time killer but has some flaws. Most important ones are;

-The reputation system. You cannot max your guy out in a single playthrough due to the achievement function so that you should abandon your game and soft reset or change leagues. And reputation is essential even if you own your club because if you don't have a good manager you never perform. This can be solved by making the +tactical achievements repeatable. 
-Financial management. Financial predictions are total gibberish thus you cannot plan ahead and balance your finance. I almost always ended up getting supporter campaign funds mid-season.
-Academy. I have had maxed out academy for a while yet it never produces any talent and it is utterly useless.
-The incidents. This one makes the game almost unplayable. Every so often you randomly get a dilemma. Some player is late for training or drunk etc. There is no way to avoid it and it is full random. This is a loss-loss situation since if you fine the player he gets unhappy, if you don't the manager gets unhappy. I have never seen one of them shrugging it off and saying "Ok my bad", even if they are model professional. They always go max unhappy. And it never gets better unless you spend points and send them on vacation or something. 

Some more minor flaws:
-You randomly get staff wanting to go on a course for like 14K points. This is completely unreasonable since it is way too expensive. If you accidentally click ok you are damned.
-After every game you get the league table on screen even if the game was a cup game.
